items.reason: Source 'kept up an incessant murdering of the sharks,*' is softened to 'slaughter'. 'Murder' is the running word of chs 65-66 ('newly murdered thing', 'murdered an ox', 'murderous jaw'); keep it.
items.new: All the same, when Stubb set the anchor-watch after finishing his supper, and Queequeg and a forecastle seaman came on deck to keep it, the sharks were thrown into no small uproar. The two men at once hung the cutting stages over the side and lowered three lanterns, which threw long gleams of light across the murky water; then, darting their long whaling-spades, they kept up a ceaseless murdering of the sharks,* driving the keen steel deep into their skulls, which seemed to be their only vital spot. But in the foaming confusion of that tangled, struggling mass, the marksmen could not always hit their target, and this revealed fresh evidence of the enemy's incredible ferocity. The sharks snapped viciously not only at one another's spilled entrails but, bending round like flexible bows, at their own, until those entrails seemed to be swallowed over and over by the same mouth, only to pass out again the opposite way through the gaping wound. Nor was that all. It was dangerous to meddle with the corpses and ghosts of these creatures. A kind of generic or Pantheistic vitality seemed to linger in their very joints and bones after what might be called their individual life had gone. One of these sharks, killed and hauled on deck for its skin, nearly took poor Queequeg's hand off when he tried to shut the dead lid of its murderous jaw.

items.reason: Source 'all the people the devil kidnapped, he'd roast for him' — 'for him' dropped, losing that the governor roasts them on the devil's behalf (the point of the bond).
items.new: "I'd like to see him try it. I'd give him such a pair of black eyes he wouldn't dare show his face in the admiral's cabin again for a good long while, let alone down in the orlop there, where he lives, or around here on the upper decks, where he sneaks about so much. Damn the devil, Flask — so you think I'm afraid of the devil? Who's afraid of him, except the old governor, who doesn't dare catch him and clap him in double-darbies — double handcuffs — as he deserves, but lets him go around kidnapping people? Yes, and he even signed a bond with him that he'd roast for him all the people the devil kidnapped. There's a governor for you!"
